pr_title: Fix nushell local env detection by using direnv export
pr_body:
I don't intend fully on getting this merged, this is just an experiment on using `direnv` directly without relying on shell-specific behaviours. It works though, so this finally closes #8633
Release Notes:

- Fixed nushell not picking up `direnv` environments by directly interfacing with it using `direnv export`

issue_context.title: Direnv environments are not picked up with either fish or nushell used
issue_context.body: ### Current status - Fish fix is merged - Nushell fix is yet to be found - Should we also ship fixes for stuff like elvish/oil/etc? ### Check for existing issues - [X] Completed ### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it The current way to pick up the environment as used in https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/dab886f4794e8d14cc82dc8e4906e93b78aa8fe8/crates/project/src/project.rs#L9366-L9385 does not work with neither fish nor nu shells. This is because direnv has some weird behaviour preventing it from evaluating. The dirty fix would be to force evaluation: ```rust let additional_command = match PathBuf::from_str(shell.as_str()) { Ok(shell_path) if shell_path.file_name() == Some(OsStr::new("fish")) => { Some("eval (direnv export fish)") } Ok(shell_path) if shell_path.file_name() == Some(OsStr::new("nu")) => { Some("direnv export json | from json | default {} | load-env") } _ => None, }; let command = match additional_command { Some(additional_command) => format!( "cd {dir:?}; {}; echo {marker}; /usr/bin/env -0; exit 0;", additional_command ), None => format!("cd {dir:?}; echo {marker}; /usr/bin/env -0; exit 0;"), }; ``` or something like that. ### Environment Zed: v0.125.1 (Zed Preview) OS: macOS 14.3.1 Memory: 8 GiB Architecture: aarch64 ### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help explain present your vision of the feature ### If applicable, attach your `~/Library/Logs/Zed/Zed.log` file to this issue. If you only need the most recent lines, you can run the `zed: open log` command palette action to see the last 1000. _No response_

review_comments: It will get loaded anyways, right? By `cd`ing into the directory. As in: I think the setting suggests an either-or decision, when it fact it's more that `ShellHook` is the default and `direct` is an additional thing, no?
If the direct option is selected, then when the shell hook is invoked, direnv would do nothing because it adds a marker environment variable to indicate that is has been activated
There's a comment on line 11744 — can you update that to include this bit here?
Why do we have to spawn a login shell with that environment? Wouldn't the better approach be to collect both environments and then merge them?

The shell does it for us, so I'm basically leveraging it's infrastructure to help us not do additional work. It also has some other upsides, imagine if someone uses direnv to install some other local environment tool, well, now we support that very specific usecase too

Yeah, it does, but is it correct? Technically you only get that `direnv` environment once you're inside the directory. Now we set it before you get to that directory and then `cd` into it. Doesn't that have the potential to mess up some other shell hooks?

If you have multiple shell hooks, I don't think their order is really determined anyways, so I think this is just equivalent to direnv executing first. As far as I know, it won't mess itself up if you already have the environment set before the `cd`, and anything else would've probably executed after it in some case anyways. The shell behaviours are sometimes strange though, so I can't guarantee that this is correct. Can we maybe try doing it and waiting for any potential bug reports, or adding this under an opt-in setting?
I've added a setting for that, defaulting to the old behaviour. I think that should resolve this issue
